newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says 1996 share gains Dfl 885 mln.
newsitem.headline: ING says 1996 share gains Dfl 885 mln.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Tuesday it realised gains of 885 million guilders on sales of shares and convertible debentures in 1996.
In a prelimary prospectus for its proposed listing on the New York Stock Exchange next month, the banking and insurance group said this compared with 178 million guilders in 1995.
ING also said it planned to offer 6.5 million American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), each of which represents an interest in one ING share, to U.S. investors.
It did not reveal the price of the ADRs.
ING said its Form F-1 registration statement, or formal prospectus, had not yet been registered by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
It said the ADRs had been bought previously through private and open-market transactions and were expected to be offered on June 12, with the listing to occur on June 13.
In the preliminary prospectus, ING has restated 1995 and 1996 profits and shareholders equity to conform with U.S. GAAP accounting principles.
It shows that 1996 net profit was 1.35 billion guilders higher than under Dutch principles at 4.67 billion.
The 1995 profit was 558 million guilders higher at 3.21 billion guilders.
The biggest boost to profit under U.S. rules are the gains on share and convertible debenture sales.
Another large gain under U.S. GAAP was profits on sales of debt securities, which totalled 354 million guilders in 1996 and 298 million in 1995.
Marking derivative financial instruments to market price boosted 1996 profit by 218 guilders in 1996 and 870 million in 1995.
Under U.S. GAAP rules however, goodwill associated with acquisitions reduced profit by 368 million guilders in 1996 and 477 million in 1995.
Losses on real estate valued at cost less depreciation cut profit by 249 million guilders in 1996 and 191 million in 1995.

ING's net charge-offs against profits for loan losses was 543 million guilders in 1996, down from 682 million in 1995, while additions to provisions for loan losses edged up to 781 million guilders from 772 million.
